thesis: Range Resources is under a definitive all-stock merger agreement with EQT (announced Oct 26, 2026): each Range share converts into 0.987 EQT shares, with closing targeted for Q1 2027. Its Q3 2026 release (Oct 27) showed operating cash flow of $308M, capital spending of $170M and production of 2.50 Bcfe per day. Range eased about 0.9% today to $55.88 on 3.2x volume, near its 52-week high. Its path appears tied to EQT's share price and the deal spread rather than to Range's own results. The Q3 10-Q flags possible merger-related shareholder suits, but none was identified, and this run found no restatement.
invalidation: The merger breaks, or a competing bid above the exchange-ratio value emerges.

thesis: Genmab rose about 28% today to $57.29 on 5.8x volume, near its 52-week high, after reporting positive topline Phase 3 results (LiGeR-HN1). The trial tested petosemtamab plus pembrolizumab in first-line PD-L1-positive head and neck cancer, met both primary endpoints, and showed a 50% reduction in the risk of death versus pembrolizumab alone. This follows the Phase 3 RAINFOL-02 success for Rina-S in ovarian cancer earlier in October. The catalyst is company-specific and confirmed, but it is topline data: full data and regulatory filings are still ahead, so approval and commercial uptake remain pending. Genmab also faces an AbbVie trade-secret suit over the Rina-S drug-linker technology and Chugai patent suits in Japan over EPKINLY; this run found no scheduled ruling in either. This run did not retrieve a company filing for the readout, which also caps this at medium.
invalidation: Full LiGeR-HN1 data reveal a safety or efficacy problem, regulators push back on a filing, or an adverse ruling in the AbbVie trade-secret case.

thesis: Axogen rose about 31% today to $49.11 on 6.2x volume after its Q3 2026 beat. Adjusted EPS was $0.21 against a ~$0.13 consensus, revenue rose 26.2% to $75.8M, and organic 2026 revenue guidance was raised to at least $283M (growth of at least 26%, from 24%). The company also expects incremental revenue from the BioCircuit acquisition, which brings an FDA-cleared sutureless nerve repair device. However, Axogen priced a $208.7M public offering of 4.91M shares on Sep 10, 2026 to fund the BioCircuit cash consideration, after a $124M offering in January. That is an equity raise inside the ~90-day window, which flags dilution risk. Law-firm investigations from 2025 over an FDA review extension have no filed claim identified.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the raised organic guidance, BioCircuit integration falters, or a further equity raise.

thesis: SELLAS fell about 14.7% today to $10.38 on 4.3x volume after announcing that its Phase 3 REGAL trial of galinpepimut-S in AML reached the planned 80 deaths, which triggers the final analysis. Topline overall-survival results are expected this quarter. Reaching the event count says nothing about efficacy, so the outcome is an unresolved binary event; commentary describes the drop as selling the news after a large 2026 run. The company is in a Hong Kong arbitration with partner 3D Medicines over roughly $13M of milestone payments, and reports of the outcome conflict. Warrant exercises raised about $28.7M earlier in the year.

Bausch Health rose about 10.1% today to $6.95 on 4.2x volume after reporting Q3 2026 and raising guidance (PR Newswire). Revenue rose 10% to $2.94B against ~$2.75B expected, adjusted EPS was $1.77 against ~$1.27, GAAP diluted EPS was $1.15, and operating cash flow more than doubled to $813M. Net debt fell by more than $500M in the quarter, and 2026 guidance was raised to revenue of $10.975-11.175B and adjusted EBITDA of $4.315-4.415B. The strongest counter-case is structural: the company carries very heavy debt (negative book value), and one quarter of paydown does not resolve that, which caps this at medium. On the legal side, a generic drug price-fixing settlement received final approval, the New Jersey securities class action was dismissed with prejudice in Nov 2025, and the Trulance patent case settled; this run found no scheduled ruling or recent restatement.
invalidation: Cash flow or debt reduction stalls, guidance is cut, or an adverse development on Xifaxan exclusivity.

thesis: ADT rose about 7.9% today to $7.415 on 3.3x volume. One report attributes the move to talks with Thrive Capital about taking the company private, while another says no company-specific catalyst was disclosed and a third points to an Oracle cloud migration plan. No agreement or company confirmation was found, so the driver is unresolved. Q3 results are due Nov 3. A March 2026 law-firm investigation after Q4 results has no filed claim. The 2023 restatement of Solar goodwill impairment falls outside the 3-year window.
invalidation: A signed, company-announced transaction with disclosed terms, or Q3 results on Nov 3 that clearly lift the outlook.

thesis: Beam rose about 15.6% today to $28.79 on 2.9x volume, just above its 200-day average. Reports tie the move to an FDA draft-guidance signal on faster routes for patient-specific gene edits, which lifted gene-editing peers (Prime Medicine was up about 20%), a sector-wide catalyst. That follows Beam's first clinical data from its BEAM-301 trial on Oct 27. The company-specific data are early, and Q3 results are due in early November. This run found no 2026 lawsuit, offering or restatement.
invalidation: Further BEAM-301 data or Q3 results that establish a company-specific path independent of the sector move.

thesis: Fortive reported Q3 2026 today (8-K). Adjusted EPS was $0.77 against a ~$0.71 consensus, core revenue grew 7.2%, and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50bp to 30.6%. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $3.10-3.14 from $2.95-3.05, and the company repurchased about $300M of stock in the quarter. The stock rose about 4.1% to $64.13 on 2.8x volume, about 4% below its 52-week high. The strongest counter-case is GAAP diluted EPS of $0.57, which missed the ~$0.61 estimate; this run could not attribute the gap between GAAP and adjusted results to a specific item, so it stays open and caps this at medium. This run found no 2026 lawsuit or restatement; a 2023 data-breach class action settled in 2025.
invalidation: Q4 results fall short of the raised guidance, or the stock closes back below its pre-report level (~$61.62).

thesis: Cheesecake Factory reported fiscal Q3 2026 on Oct 27 (8-K). Revenue was $1,033.4M against $907.2M a year earlier, comparable sales at Cheesecake Factory restaurants rose 15.2%, adjusted EPS of $1.02 topped estimates of about $0.91-0.94, and the $0.30 dividend was maintained. The stock nonetheless slipped about 2.5% today to $105.78 on 2.7x volume, about 11% below its 52-week high. Coverage attributes the dip to the outlook and continued reinvestment spending. That margin counter-case is named but not resolved by this run's research, which caps this at medium. This run found no 2026 lawsuit or restatement; a $125K SEC settlement dates to 2020.
invalidation: Margins compress enough to offset the sales growth, or the stock keeps falling after the report.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 19). Avantor reported Q3 2026 this morning (8-K). Net sales rose 4.6% to $1,698.3M with 5.2% organic growth, adjusted EPS of $0.22 beat the ~$0.21 consensus, free cash flow was $156.2M, and the company raised its 2026 organic growth, adjusted EPS and free-cash-flow guidance. That resolves the prior thesis's Q3 binary-event counter-case in the thesis's favor. The stock still fell about 2.6% to $16.68 on 3.2x volume, and adjusted EBITDA (-4.1%) and adjusted EPS (-3.0%) declined year over year, so margins have not yet followed sales. The other counter-case from the prior thesis remains open: the motion to dismiss the securities class action has no ruling date. This stays medium.
invalidation: Q4 results fall short of the raised guidance, an adverse class-action ruling, or a close back below the 20-day average.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF edged up about 0.3% today to $13.935, above the ~$12.12 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report: adjusted EBITDA of $612M against $575M guidance, Q4 guided to about $715M, and 2027 guided above $4B. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open. The outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, and the Hamilton (Stelco) layoffs confirmed Oct 21 point to tariff pressure on the Canadian unit. This stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 1.5% to $37.105, above its ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY Phase 3 results for brepocitinib in non-infectious uveitis. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027, so approval for this indication and its commercial weight are still pending. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 26). RNG rose about 0.8% to $86.27, and this run found no new company disclosure. The thesis rests on the Oct 22 Q3 2026 report (8-K). Revenue rose 5.9% to $676M, above the $664-670M guidance, and the non-GAAP operating margin reached 24.7%, up about 190bp. Full-year guidance was raised to $2.650-2.657B in revenue, $5.07-5.12 in non-GAAP EPS and $620-630M in free cash flow. ARR from customers using a paid AI product doubled to nearly 15% of the total. The strongest counter-case is competitive: growth is only about 6% in a crowded cloud-communications market. That doesn't change the read, because the beat, the margin expansion and the raised EPS and free-cash-flow guidance all come from the company's own disclosed results at that growth rate. This is the counter-case named and resolved in the prior thesis, and no new fact reopens it. A January 2026 law-firm investigation notice has no filed claim, the 10-Q shows no material proceeding, and the next earnings report is about four months away (Feb 2027).
invalidation: Q4 revenue or margin falls short of the raised guidance, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$79.42).

thesis: Held position (opened today, Oct 28). Centene fell about 2.4% today to $67.03, closing back below its ~$68.03 pre-report level. That meets one of the prior thesis's invalidation criteria, and this run found no new company disclosure explaining the move. The Oct 27 Q3 report (8-K) still stands: adjusted EPS of $0.58 against a consensus near $0.07-0.10, full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to above $5.20, and Medicare Advantage now expected to break even in 2026. But the market has reversed the post-report gain, and the counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open. Those are Medicaid margins (93.6% benefits ratio, with management expecting membership declines and acuity shifts to slow recovery through 2027) and a GAAP loss of $0.14 per share not attributed to a specific charge. The read is therefore unresolved. The early-exit guard applies, since there is no fact newer than the entry thesis, so this stays long at low conviction. A securities class action (Lunstrum v. Centene, S.D.N.Y.) has no scheduled ruling identified.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or further declines below the pre-report level on new adverse disclosures.
